text:
alice_ops: heads-up — seeing a repeating latency sawtooth pattern in eu-west dedicated pools over the last ~3h. 95p token latency jumps ~2.5-3x every ~6–8m, aligns with egress queue depth spikes. posting screenshots: https://grafana/repl/graphs/abc123 :eyes:
ben_infra: can you paste the prometheus query you used? curious if it's per-pool or per-tenant
alice_ops: query I used: `sum by(pool) (rate(redwood_inference_token_latency_seconds_sum[1m])) / sum by(pool) (rate(redwood_inference_token_latency_seconds_count[1m]))` — overlayed with `sum by(pool) (redwood_egress_queue_depth)` shows correlation
dmitri_net: I pulled tcp_ring metrics on the affected nodes — TX ring full and netdev backlog spikes when the sawtooth hits. Kernel 6.1 patch rolled in last week; possible qdisc/tc interactions. also seeing increased softirq counts on nic0
carmen_sre: I routed a small subset of streaming embedding traffic to the burst queue pool ~30m ago as an experiment. tail latencies dropped for that subset but preempt counts on the burst pool rose (evictions). so we reduced surface but moved pressure elsewhere :grimacing:
ben_infra: hypothesis: long-lived TLS streaming sessions with steady small batches are starving prefix/KV cache locality and creating repeated cache thrash + egress queueing. two levers: per-tenant egress token-bucket on the sidecar OR stronger warm-pool-affinity to keep those sessions pinned to warm slices
alice_ops: sidecar throttle sounds less disruptive to existing allocation logic. can we implement a soft token-bucket (bursty) so interactive short calls unaffected but sustained streams get smoothed?
dmitri_net: we can add tc ingress policing on the sidecar interface or BPF qdisc to shape per-conn sustained bandwidth. more robust long-term: flow-classify streams with conn-duration > Xs and tag for dedicated egress NIC/route
ben_infra: config snippet for soft token-bucket (sidecar):
```
sidecar.network.egress_rate_limit:
  mode: token_bucket
  rate: 200mbit
  burst: 50mbit
  per_tenant: true
  window_seconds: 60
```
apply as a feature-flag to eu-west first
carmen_sre: cost note — if we go with dedicated egress NICs / dedicated pools for long streams we should add tenant billing tags. otherwise committed capacity will eat margins.
alice_ops: test plan: roll token-bucket as canary to eu-west-a for 5% of tenants running streaming embeddings, monitor 95/99/99.9 latencies, egress_queue_depth, gpu_preempt_count. rollback if preempt_count rises > 20% or 95p lat > baseline * 1.5
deploy-bot: prod-deploy start: canary/eu-west-a tokenbucket-v1 -> 2634513600 by ben_infra
dmitri_net: I'll tail netdev and softirq while canary runs, and toss up tc rules if we need immediate mitigation
ben_infra: if canary good, follow-up: add warm-pool-affinity flag to allocator and experiment with a small reserved slab for long-lived streams (soft-reserve, allow bursting)
alice_ops: filed infra-ticket RW-3178 with canary details and rollback playbook: https://redwood.atlassian/RW-3178 — starting canary in ~10m. ping me if you see anything odd :thumbsup:
